prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Dollar Shave Club (company_id dollar-shave-club; category: razors and grooming subscription)
Official domains: dollarshaveclub.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://www.brandcredential.com/post/the-dollar-shave-club-marketing-strategy-a-comprehensive-analysis | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Utilizing Social Media for Brand Awareness The Dollar Shave Club recognized the potential of social media in building brand awareness and engaged with their target audience through various platforms. By consistently creating compelling content, interacting with followers, and partnering with influencers, the brand was able to foster a strong and loyal community of advocates who amplified their message across the digital landscape. Through their social media presence, the Dollar Shave Club has been able to establish a personal connection with their customers. They actively respond to comments and messages, making their followers feel heard and valued."

[P2] source: https://www.brandcredential.com/post/the-dollar-shave-club-marketing-strategy-a-comprehensive-analysis | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"This level of engagement has not only helped to build trust but has also encouraged customers to become brand ambassadors, spreading the word about the Dollar Shave Club to their own networks. The brand's partnerships with influencers have played a crucial role in expanding their reach. By collaborating with individuals who have a large following and align with their target audience, the Dollar Shave Club has been able to tap into new markets and gain exposure to potential customers who may not have otherwise discovered the brand."

[P3] source: https://www.projectpractical.com/dollar-shave-club-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Dollar Shave Club’s success can be attributed to its viral marketing campaign, unique value proposition, memorable branding, and targeted messaging. * The company’s subscription-based business model offered affordability and convenience, disrupting the traditional retail razor market. * Dollar Shave Club’s humorous marketing and relatable content set them apart from competitors and helped build a strong brand identity. * Social media engagement and an emphasis on excellent customer service contributed to high customer satisfaction and loyalty."

[P4] source: https://www.projectpractical.com/dollar-shave-club-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Social Media Engagement Dollar Shave Club recognized the power of social media marketing and utilized platforms like Facebook and Twitter to engage with their customers effectively. By leveraging these channels, they were able to create a strong sense of community around their brand and foster brand loyalty. One of the key strategies Dollar Shave Club implemented was sharing user-generated content on their social media profiles. This not only showcased the satisfaction and enthusiasm of their customers but also encouraged others to participate and share their experiences."

[P5] source: https://www.projectpractical.com/dollar-shave-club-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Furthermore, Dollar Shave Club leveraged social media platforms like Facebook and Twitter to engage with their customers, cultivate a sense of community, and create personalized experiences. By providing exceptional customer service, including a satisfaction guarantee and easy cancellation options, they cultivated trust and loyalty among their customer base. By studying and applying the key elements of Dollar Shave Club’s marketing strategy, marketers can gain valuable insights into building effective campaigns that connect with their target audience."

[P6] source: https://www.capitalism.com/dollar-shave-club/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Takeaway The founders of DSC launched their razor subscription business to meet a specific customer need. They understood success takes more than a fantastic product. It's crucial to know the target audience and ensure the product solves a problem for the ideal customer. Although they spent their first eight months building their new business in an apartment, Michael Dubin and Mark Levine knew they had something special. So they used their skills to create a viral video campaign that took the razor industry by storm, engaged customers and investors, and paved the way for other direct-to-consumer brands."

[P7] source: https://www.brandcredential.com/post/the-dollar-shave-club-marketing-strategy-a-comprehensive-analysis | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The Power of Viral Marketing One of the most significant factors behind the Dollar Shave Club's rapid rise to prominence is its effective use of viral marketing. The brand's launch video, featuring the charismatic founder, captivated millions of viewers and quickly garnered widespread attention. The video's humorous and relatable tone struck a chord with viewers, making it highly shareable. As a result, the Dollar Shave Club leveraged the power of social media to spread their message like wildfire. But it wasn't just the video itself that propelled the brand forward. The Dollar Shave Club understood the importance of creating content that resonated with their target audience."

[P8] source: https://www.capitalism.com/dollar-shave-club/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"What are the benefits of using Dollar Shave Club? DSC offers several benefits to customers. Subscriptions come with free shipping, discounts up to 15%, birthday rewards, and early access to new product launches. But ultimately, the convenience and affordability of DSC are the biggest benefits that have created long-term, loyal customers for the brand."

[P9] source: https://www.capitalism.com/dollar-shave-club/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"1: Start Where You Are Michael Dubin launched DSC from his apartment. Having a big office or staff is unnecessary to create a lucrative ecommerce brand."

[P10] source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/Da0arCpyfvM/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Follow Original audio More options marketingtinder's profile picture marketingtinder Verified 17w This legendary launch video by Dollar Shave Club is a masterclass in how to disrupt a billion-dollar industry through raw, unfiltered storytelling. Instead of showing slow-motion water droplets or unnecessary \"shave tech,\" the brand used dry, brutal honesty to target a real consumer frustration overpriced razors. By calling out the industry's ridiculous features and offering a dead-simple solution, they built an instant connection. It perfectly delivers the core hook: \"Our blades are f***ing great."

generator.quote_repair: claims.repair_quotes (min similarity 0.9; numbers/negations unchanged); see attempts[].quote_repairs
generator.note: unsupported claims and every sentence citing them were removed automatically (auto_threshold_0.7)

hints_shown: Every {C#} marker must refer to a claim in the claims list; remove or fix dangling markers.
Claims the reviewer did not find supported: delete them and every sentence that cites them, or replace the quote with one that directly states the claim.
